title: Rush Rate Where the Promise Has Passed or a Goodwill Recovery Stands
content:
# Service Training Note: The Rush Rate Where the Promise Has Passed or a Goodwill Recovery Stands

## The rule the desk applies

The rush rate carried on a work order of the Belrose Workshop Repair and Resizing Service is stepped down by reference to two records on that order: whether the promised date has passed at the handling date, and whether an amount has already been taken off the order as a goodwill recovery.

1. Where the promised date has passed and an amount has already been taken off the work order as a goodwill recovery, the rush rate is the level's rush share less the recovery step of 8 percent.
2. Where exactly one of those two holds — the promised date has passed and no goodwill recovery stands on the order, or a goodwill recovery stands and the promised date has not passed — the rush rate is the level's rush share less the standing step of 4 percent.
3. In any other case the rush rate is the level's rush share, not stepped down on these grounds.

Where the level carries no rush share, or the step taken off the rush share would take it below nothing, the rush rate is nothing.

## Questions answered

**Which amounts count as a goodwill recovery?** Those taken off the work order as a goodwill service recovery. An amount taken off under a member benefit, or under the workmanship guarantee, is not one.

**When has the promised date passed?** When the handling date is later than the day standing on the work order as the day the piece is promised back. A promised date falling on the handling date itself has not passed.

**What if the step would take the rate below nothing?** Then the rush rate is nothing, and no expedited charge follows from the rate.

**Hypothetical readings.** At a level whose rush share is 25 percent: with the promise passed and a goodwill recovery standing, the rush rate is 17 percent; with the promise passed and no goodwill recovery, 21 percent; with a goodwill recovery and the promise not passed, 21 percent; with neither, 25 percent. At a level whose rush share is 0 percent, the rush rate is nothing in every one of those cases.
